docs.title: Why Takwin?
docs.text:
Lightning-Fast Build Tool

  • Instant startup: ~50ms startup time
  • Single binary: No runtime dependencies or complex installations
  • Cross-platform: Native support for Linux, macOS, and Windows
  • Enterprise-ready: Comprehensive testing, CI/CD, and security scanning

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Linux/macOSWindowsDocker 
# Download and install
curl -L https://github.com/hakkim/takwin/releases/latest/download/takwin-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar -xz
sudo mv takwin-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/takwin

# Verify installation
takwin --version

# Download from releases
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/hakkim/takwin/releases/latest/download/takwin-windows-amd64.zip" -OutFile "takwin.zip"
Expand-Archive -Path "takwin.zip" -DestinationPath "C:\Program Files\Takwin"

# Add to PATH and verify
takwin --version

# Pull the image
docker pull ghcr.io/hakkim/takwin:latest

# Run in current directory
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace -w /workspace ghcr.io/hakkim/takwin:latest build

docs.title: Your First Build
docs.text:
Create a simple C++ project:

# Create project directory
mkdir hello-world && cd hello-world

# Create source file
cat > main.cpp << EOF
#include <iostream>
int main() {
    std::cout << "Hello, Takwin!" << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
EOF

# Create build configuration
cat > build.toml << EOF
[project]
name = "hello"
version = "1.0.0"

[[targets]]
name = "hello"
type = "executable"
sources = ["main.cpp"]
EOF

# Build and run
takwin build
./build/bin/hello

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This document describes the internal architecture of Takwin.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Takwin is built with a clean, modular architecture using Go's interface-based design patterns.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
takwin/
├── main.go                      # Entry point
├── cmd/                         # CLI commands (Cobra)
│   ├── root.go                  # Root command
│   ├── build.go                 # Build command
│   ├── clean.go                 # Clean command
│   └── list.go                  # List command
├── internal/
│   ├── config/                  # Configuration handling
│   │   ├── config.go            # TOML loading & validation
│   │   └── config_test.go       # Tests
│   ├── build/
│   │   ├── engine.go            # Build orchestration
│   │   └── engine_test.go       # Tests
│   ├── compiler/
│   │   ├── adapter.go           # Compiler implementations
│   │   └── adapter_test.go      # Tests
│   ├── platform/
│   │   └── adapter.go           # Platform-specific code
│   └── sources/
│       ├── resolver.go          # File pattern resolution
│       └── resolver_test.go     # Tests
├── examples/                    # Example projects
├── docs/                        # Documentation
└── go.mod                       # Go module definition

docs.title: 1. CLI Layer (cmd/)
docs.text:
Built with Cobra, provides the command-line interface.

Commands: - build - Build project targets - clean - Clean build artifacts - list-targets - List available targets

docs.title: 2. Configuration (internal/config/)
docs.text:
Handles TOML configuration parsing and validation.

Key Types: 

type Config struct {
    Project Project
    Build   Build
    Targets []Target
}

Responsibilities: - Parse build.toml files - Validate configuration - Provide target lookup

docs.title: 3. Build Engine (internal/build/)
docs.text:
Orchestrates the build process.

Key Type: 

type Engine struct {
    config   *config.Config
    compiler compiler.Adapter
    platform platform.Adapter
    resolver sources.Resolver
}

Responsibilities: - Coordinate build process - Resolve source files - Generate compiler commands - Manage output directories

docs.title: 4. Compiler Adapters (internal/compiler/)
docs.text:
Provides abstraction over different compilers.

Interface: 

type Adapter interface {
    Name() string
    SupportsLanguage(lang string) bool
    BuildCompileCommand(ctx *Context) []string
    BuildStaticLibraryCommand(ctx *Context) []string
}

Implementations: - GCC Adapter - Clang Adapter - MSVC Adapter

docs.title: 5. Platform Adapters (internal/platform/)
docs.text:
Handles platform-specific behavior.

Responsibilities: - Add platform-specific file extensions - Handle path separators - Platform detection

docs.title: 6. Source Resolver (internal/sources/)
docs.text:
Resolves source file patterns to actual files.

Implementations: - Glob Resolver - Pattern matching - Explicit Resolver - Direct file lists - Smart Resolver - Combination of both

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[CLI Command] --> B[Parse Config]
    B --> C[Create Build Engine]
    C --> D[Resolve Sources]
    D --> E[Select Compiler]
    E --> F[Generate Commands]
    F --> G[Execute Build]
    G --> H[Output Artifacts]

docs.title: 1. Adapter Pattern
docs.text:
Used for compiler and platform abstraction:

// Compiler interface
type Adapter interface {
    BuildCompileCommand(ctx *Context) []string
}

// GCC implementation
type GccAdapter struct{}
func (g *GccAdapter) BuildCompileCommand(ctx *Context) []string {
    // GCC-specific implementation
}

// Clang implementation
type ClangAdapter struct{}
func (c *ClangAdapter) BuildCompileCommand(ctx *Context) []string {
    // Clang-specific implementation
}

docs.title: 2. Strategy Pattern
docs.text:
Used for source file resolution:

type Resolver interface {
    Resolve(patterns []string, excludePatterns []string) ([]string, error)
}

// Different strategies
type GlobResolver struct{}
type ExplicitResolver struct{}
type SmartResolver struct{}

docs.title: 3. Builder Pattern
docs.text:
Used for constructing build contexts:

type Context struct {
    Sources      []string
    Output       string
    TargetType   TargetType
    IncludePaths []string
    Libraries    []string
    // ...
}

# Solution: List available targets
takwin list-targets

$ takwin build

# Solution: Install compiler or specify different one

# Create header file
mkdir include
cat > include/math_utils.h << EOF
#pragma once

int add(int a, int b);
int multiply(int a, int b);
EOF

# Create source files
mkdir src
cat > src/math_utils.cpp << EOF
#include "math_utils.h"

int add(int a, int b) {
    return a + b;
}

int multiply(int a, int b) {
    return a * b;
}
EOF

cat > src/main.cpp << EOF
#include <iostream>
#include "math_utils.h"

int main() {
    std::cout << "5 + 3 = " << add(5, 3) << std::endl;
    std::cout << "5 * 3 = " << multiply(5, 3) << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
EOF

# Create build configuration
cat > build.toml << EOF
[project]
name = "math_project"
version = "1.0.0"

[build]
compiler = "gcc"
optimization = "O2"
include_paths = ["include"]

[[targets]]
name = "math_app"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/*.cpp"]
EOF

takwin build

[project]
name = "library_project"
version = "1.0.0"

[build]
compiler = "gcc"
optimization = "O2"
include_paths = ["include"]

# Static library target
[[targets]]
name = "mathlib"
type = "static_library"
sources = ["src/math_utils.cpp"]
output = "math"

# Executable target using the library
[[targets]]
name = "app"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/main.cpp"]
libraries = ["math"]
library_paths = ["build/lib"]
EOF

# Build library first, then executable
takwin build -t mathlib
takwin build -t app

docs.title: What is Takwin?
docs.text: Takwin is a modern, fast build tool for C and C++ projects. It uses simple TOML configuration files instead of complex Makefiles.

docs.title: Why use Takwin instead of Make/CMake?
docs.text:
• Simpler: TOML configuration vs complex Makefile syntax
  • Faster: ~50ms startup time
  • Single binary: No dependencies to install
  • Cross-platform: Works on Linux, macOS, Windows
  • Modern: Built with Go for reliability

docs.title: Is Takwin production-ready?
docs.text: Takwin is currently in beta (v0.1.0-beta.1). It's suitable for: - ✅ Personal projects - ✅ Small to medium projects - ✅ Evaluation and testing - ⚠️ Production use (with caution)

docs.title: What license is Takwin under?
docs.text: MIT License - free for commercial and personal use.

docs.title: How do I install Takwin?
docs.text:
See the Installation Guide for detailed instructions.

Quick install: 

curl -L https://github.com/hakkim/takwin/releases/latest/download/takwin-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar -xz
sudo mv takwin-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/takwin

docs.title: Do I need to install any dependencies?
docs.text: No! Takwin is a single binary with no runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Can I use Takwin with Docker?
docs.text:
Yes! We provide official Docker images: 

docker pull ghcr.io/hakkim/takwin:latest

docs.title: How do I create a build configuration?
docs.text:
Create a build.toml file: 

[project]
name = "myproject"
version = "1.0.0"

[[targets]]
name = "myapp"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/*.cpp"]

docs.title: What compilers does Takwin support?
docs.text:
• GCC
  • Clang
  • MSVC (Windows)

docs.title: Can I use Takwin for C projects?
docs.text: Yes! Takwin supports both C and C++ projects.

docs.title: How do I build multiple targets?
docs.text:
Define multiple [[targets]] sections: 

[[targets]]
name = "mylib"
type = "static_library"
sources = ["lib/*.cpp"]

[[targets]]
name = "myapp"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/*.cpp"]
libraries = ["mylib"]

docs.title: Can I use glob patterns for source files?
docs.text:
Yes! Takwin supports glob patterns: 

sources = ["src/**/*.cpp"]  # Recursive
sources = ["src/*.cpp"]     # Single directory
sources = ["src/main.cpp", "src/utils.cpp"]  # Explicit files

docs.title: Where should I put my build.toml?
docs.text: In your project root directory, next to your source code.

docs.title: Can I use a different config file name?
docs.text:
Yes, use the --config flag: 

takwin build --config my-config.toml

docs.title: How do I set compiler flags?
docs.text:
[build]
compile_flags = ["-Wall", "-Wextra", "-std=c++17"]
link_flags = ["-static"]

include_paths = ["include", "third_party/include"]

docs.title: How do I link libraries?
docs.text:

libraries = ["pthread", "m"]
library_paths = ["/usr/local/lib"]

docs.text: Not yet. This is planned for v0.2.0.

docs.title: Can I run tests with Takwin?
docs.text:
Takwin focuses on building. Use your test framework separately: 

takwin build
./build/bin/tests

docs.title: Does Takwin support cross-compilation?
docs.text:
Yes! Set the target platform: 

GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 takwin build

docs.title: Multi-File Project
docs.text:
Create a more complex project:

mkdir math-project && cd math-project

# Create header file
mkdir include
cat > include/math_utils.h << EOF
#pragma once

int add(int a, int b);
int multiply(int a, int b);
EOF

# Create source files
mkdir src
cat > src/math_utils.cpp << EOF
#include "math_utils.h"

int add(int a, int b) {
    return a + b;
}

int multiply(int a, int b) {
    return a * b;
}
EOF

cat > src/main.cpp << EOF
#include <iostream>
#include "math_utils.h"

int main() {
    std::cout << "5 + 3 = " << add(5, 3) << std::endl;
    std::cout << "5 * 3 = " << multiply(5, 3) << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
EOF

# Create build configuration
cat > build.toml << EOF
[project]
name = "math_project"
version = "1.0.0"

[build]
compiler = "gcc"
optimization = "O2"
include_paths = ["include"]

[[targets]]
name = "math_app"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/*.cpp"]
EOF

# Build and run
takwin build
./build/bin/math_app

docs.title: Library Project
docs.text:
Create a project with both library and executable:

mkdir library-project && cd library-project

# Create the same structure as above, then:
cat > build.toml << EOF
[project]
name = "library_project"
version = "1.0.0"

[build]
compiler = "gcc"
optimization = "O2"
include_paths = ["include"]

# Static library target
[[targets]]
name = "mathlib"
type = "static_library"
sources = ["src/math_utils.cpp"]
output = "math"

# Executable target using the library
[[targets]]
name = "app"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/main.cpp"]
libraries = ["math"]
library_paths = ["build/lib"]
EOF

# Build library first, then executable
takwin build -t mathlib
takwin build -t app

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
[project]
name = "my_project"
version = "1.0.0"

[build]
compiler = "gcc"           # gcc, clang, msvc
optimization = "O2"        # O0, O1, O2, O3, Os
output_dir = "build"

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
[project]
name = "advanced_project"
version = "2.0.0"

[build]
compiler = "gcc"
optimization = "O2"
output_dir = "build"
include_paths = ["include", "third_party/include"]
libraries = ["pthread", "m"]
compile_flags = ["-Wall", "-Wextra", "-std=c++17"]
link_flags = ["-static"]

[[targets]]
name = "my_app"
type = "executable"
sources = ["src/main.cpp", "src/utils.cpp"]
include_paths = ["app/include"]  # Target-specific includes
libraries = ["boost_system"]     # Target-specific libraries
compile_flags = ["-DAPP_VERSION=\"2.0.0\""]

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common issues and solutions for Takwin users.

docs.title: Binary Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: takwin: command not found

Solution: 

# Ensure binary is in PATH
echo $PATH

# Add to PATH (Linux/macOS)
export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/bin

# Or move binary to PATH location
sudo mv takwin /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
Problem: Permission denied when running takwin

Solution: 

# Make binary executable
chmod +x takwin

# Or run with sudo for installation
sudo mv takwin /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: Compiler Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: gcc: command not found or clang: command not found

Solution:

LinuxmacOSWindows 
# Install GCC
sudo apt-get install build-essential

# Or Clang
sudo apt-get install clang

# Install Xcode Command Line Tools
xcode-select --install

# Or install via Homebrew
brew install gcc

# Install MinGW
choco install mingw

# Or install MSVC via Visual Studio

docs.title: Source Files Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: no source files found for target

Solution: 1. Check glob patterns in build.toml 2. Verify file paths are correct 3. Use absolute paths or relative to project root

[[targets]]
name = "myapp"
sources = ["src/*.cpp"]  # Check this pattern

docs.title: Build Fails Silently
docs.text:
Problem: Build completes but no output

Solution: 

# Run with verbose output
takwin build -v

# Check output directory
ls -la build/

docs.title: Invalid TOML Syntax
docs.text:
Problem: failed to parse build.toml

Solution: - Check TOML syntax - Validate with online TOML validator - Common issues: - Missing quotes around strings - Incorrect array syntax - Duplicate keys

# ❌ Wrong
[project]
name = hello  # Missing quotes

# ✅ Correct
[project]
name = "hello"

docs.title: Target Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: target 'xyz' not found

Solution: 

# List available targets
takwin list-targets

# Check target name in build.toml
[[targets]]
name = "correct_name"  # Use this name

docs.title: Slow Build Times
docs.text:
Solutions: 1. Use optimization flags 2. Enable parallel builds (when available) 3. Use incremental builds (when available)

[build]
optimization = "O2"  # Use appropriate level

docs.title: High Memory Usage
docs.text: Solutions: 1. Build targets individually 2. Reduce parallel jobs 3. Close other applications

docs.title: Windows: Path Issues
docs.text:
Problem: Paths with spaces or special characters

Solution: 

# Use forward slashes
sources = ["C:/Program Files/project/src/*.cpp"]

# Or escape backslashes
sources = ["C:\\Program Files\\project\\src\\*.cpp"]

docs.title: macOS: Code Signing
docs.text:
Problem: "Developer cannot be verified"

Solution: 

# Remove quarantine attribute
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine takwin

# Or allow in System Preferences > Security & Privacy

docs.title: Linux: Library Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: error while loading shared libraries

Solution: 

# Update library cache
sudo ldconfig

# Or set LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/libs:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
